interface_detail: a public *.azurewebsites.net endpoint; deployment by git, zip or container
tooling: the Azure CLI, Kudu, git push deployment
chaining: a public HTTPS endpoint with 60 CPU minutes a day, which is a scheduler and not a host

limits.value: 60 CPU minutes a day shared across the app
the app sleeps after 20 minutes without a direct request; Always On is not available on F1
1 GB RAM and 1.00 GB of storage

limits_note: the 20-minute idle timeout is stated by Microsoft in two first-party articles; learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/webjobs-execution carries the sentence quoted in evidence
notes: It is documented first-party at learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/webjobs-execution (read 2026-10-22), which also says a portal visit or a Kudu request does not reset the timer

free_tier.stated: F1 Free Shared: 60 CPU minutes a day, 1 GB RAM, 1.00 GB storage, no SLA
free_tier.notes: the 512 MB and 5 GB figures in older guides are obsolete

retention.stated: the app and its files persist on the plan; no deletion clock is stated

egress.terms: the App Service pricing page states no F1 data-transfer line; Azure bandwidth pricing gives the first 100 GB/month free, then USD 0.087 per GB from North America or Europe
egress.free_allowance: first 100 GB per month of internet egress free (Azure bandwidth pricing, not an App Service F1 line)

identity_cost.detail: an Azure account requires a card and a phone number

session_cap.note: 20-minute idle timeout: 'Web apps can time out after 20 minutes of inactivity, and only direct requests to the app reset this idle timer. Actions like viewing the portal or accessing the Kudu tools don't keep the app active.'

keep_rate.basis: a free app does not bill

binding_note: the 20-minute idle timer is the first wall: 60 CPU-minutes a day is generous for a keepalive, and a keepalive needs a direct request to reset the timer, which a health probe from outside the app supplies
